column1: # What paraglider line is made of, from the people who make and test it.
# line-materials.tsv gives strengths and diameters and does not say which
# fibre a line is. The model guessed from the name, and guessed the two most
# used families backwards: Edelrid's 8000-U and 8001 are aramid and were
# classed as Dyneema; Liros's PPSL is Dyneema under a polyester cover and was
# classed as aramid. This file is the record the classification is held to.
#   ED-7343   Edelrid technical data sheet "2 7343 HELIX", 2025
#   ED-6843   Edelrid technical data sheet "2 6843 CARVEX", 2025
#   ED-7850   Edelrid technical data sheet "2 7850 TARAX", 2025
#   ED-7950   Edelrid technical data sheet "2 7950 MATRIX", 2025
#   ED-8001   Edelrid product page, MAGIX PRO DRY (article 8001): "hydrophobic,
#   DHV-452   DHV line test report LI 452-2016, Edelrid 8000-U type 190:
#   DHV-1042  DHV line test report LI 1042.2021, Edelrid 9200-035:
#   LIROS-24  LIROS flight sport brochure 2024: PPSL, PPSLS and DSL "core
#             pre-stretched Dyneema, cover polyester"; DFL Dyneema under
#             polyester; LTC "100 % Technora", no cover; TSL Technora under
#   COUSIN    Cousin Trestec paraglider line brochure: Vectraline "100 %
#             Vectran single braid", Technoline "100 % Technora single braid"
#   NIVIUK-L3 Niviuk technical data, Link 3: every suspension line a TNL
#             (80 to 400) supplied by Teijin Limited, Japan — the maker of
#             Technora — and the brake line Edelrid's TARAX-240
# Part 1 — families. `core` is what carries the load; `cover` is "none" for a
# line that is braided and coated without a sheath. `basis` is "stated" where
# the source names the fibre, and "inferred" where it is read from the name
# and from how much strength the line keeps when kinked.

column7: keeps 52 % kinked, as the Technora lines do; not in LIROS-24
COUSIN names the family; V12-100 and V16-140 read as its 12100 and 16140
